title: One bee makes a lot of honey?

segments.text: Bees are so busy, one bee must make tons of honey. Well, that's not exactly true. In its whole life, a worker bee makes about one twelfth of a teaspoon.
So to fill one jar, a colony visits around two million flowers. And together they fly about twice around the Earth.
Here's the wild part. Bees carry nectar in a second stomach, called a honey stomach. It's basically a tiny backpack inside their body.
In fact, bees tell each other where the flowers are by dancing. The direction of the waggle points the way, and its length tells the distance.
That's not all. Their wings beat around {200|two hundred} times a second. That's the buzz you hear.
And honey almost never spoils. Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs, thousands of years old.
So one bee makes just a tiny drop of honey. But together, they make something that lasts forever.
